Then the 1- and 2-minute people have to shuttle the torch back and forth, and the best arrangement gives 2+1+10+2+2=17, versus 19 if the 1-minute person just escorts everyone individually.

The optimal schedule for people 1, 2, 5, and 10 minutes: send 1 and 2 across together, 1 returns, then 5 and 10 cross together, 2 returns, and finally 1 and 2 cross again — totaling 17 minutes. The reasoning for optimality is that pairing the two slowest together avoids wasting their time individually, and alternatives like having person 1 escort everyone one at a time take longer (19 minutes); the lower bound confirms 17 is unbeatable since at least three two-person forward crossings are required, two of them involving the fastest pair.

2+2+10+1+2 = 17 — crossing in a different order: 1&2 cross, 2 returns, 5&10 cross, 1 returns, 1&2 cross. Equally valid alternative achieving the same total.

I'll present a short table with the step order and times, then explain the reasoning.

**The fastest total time is 17 minutes.**

## Schedule

| Step | Move | Time | Elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 and 2 cross | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 1 returns with the torch | 1 | 3 |
| 3 | 5 and 10 cross | 10 | 13 |
| 4 | 2 returns with the torch | 2 | 15 |
| 5 | 1 and 2 cross | 2 | 17 |

The idea is to send the two slowest people together, so their times overlap instead of adding, and to use the two fastest people to ferry the torch back. Swapping the order of steps 1–2 and 3–4 also gives 17 (1 and 2 cross, 2 returns, 5 and 10 cross, 1 returns, 1 and 2 cross).

The obvious alternative, where the 1-minute person escorts everyone, takes 10 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 2 = 19 minutes.

## Why 17 can't be beaten

- Getting four people across needs at least 5 crossings (3 forward, 2 back), and at least three of the forward crossings must carry two people.
- If the 5 and the 10 cross on separate trips, those two trips cost at least 15. The other three or more crossings cost at least 1 each, so the total is at least 18.
- So the 5 and 10 cross together, costing 10. The other two two-person forward trips cost 2 only if both are the pair {1, 2}. Any other pair includes the 5 or 10 and costs at least 5, which makes the total at least 10 + 2 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 19.
- If both trips are {1, 2}, then the 2-minute person crosses forward twice, so he must come back once (at least 2 min). The other return costs at least 1 min. The total is at least 10 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 17.

So 17 minutes is optimal.
